links.comparator_used: Hospital-only baseline model trained on real hospital data only (vs. synthetic-pretrained zero-shot and domain-adapted models)
links.outcome: 7-year overall survival prediction, AUPRC and Brier score on held-out real hospital test set
links.effect: Domain adaptation (synthetic pretraining then local fine-tuning) improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations, 4 statistically significant; best XGBoost+RUS+F1 AUPRC=0.5391 (Δ+0.1474; P<.001). Zero-shot use of the synthetic-pretrained model reduced AUPRC in most settings, with no significant gains elsewhere. Brier scores improved in most domain adaptation combinations.
links.tradeoff: Synthetic data did not substitute for real data: zero-shot use of the synthetic-pretrained model performed worse, and the authors conclude synthetic data is a complement, not a substitute, for local clinical data.
links.quote: In contrast, the domain adaptation model improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations, with 4 statistically significant gains; the best setting (XGBoost+RUS+F1 optimization) achieved AUPRC=0.5391 (Δ+0.1474; P<.001).
